summary: Proceed: E passes (fresh at 1.6340 / blob 2eb03f76; this is the judge check that CLAIMS.md:86 [lead] names as its reopen), and the in-prepare race with a <=0.95 bar caps the downside at the cost of one check. Expect the H100 edge to shrink on the H200: realistic e2e about 0.86-0.92 and a 2-3.5% headline, not 4.2%. The build has to remove a grid-barrier hang risk and gate on page_size/kv_scale.
justification: The mechanism holds up on this SM. FA3's full-verify main loop is limited by memory parallelism per SM (CLAIMS.md:84: one CTA/SM, 24-32 KB in flight, 2.04 TB/s, DRAM 62.5%). The gate keeps 64 KB/SM in flight, and in the same process with interleaved cold-L2 rounds over 2 seeds its mainloop beat FA3's main kernel 1.22-1.24x (259 vs 322 us at v32, 137-139 vs 167-171 at v16). End to end it was 0.82 / 0.83-0.84 of master's call, with tolerance held and 23x more accurate than FA3 vs fp32. It differs from the earlier custom full-verify loops that lost on the judge in four measured ways (s3-s7, FINDINGS:177-189, CLAIMS.md:63; s6's DIAG was 179/367 us vs FA3 148.6/285.9). (1) FP8 QK uses wgmma. mma.sync e4m3 is emulated on sm_90a (F2FP unpack + 2 HMMA; v1 of the lineage ran 467 us). (2) Lean load issue, about 140 fewer instr/warp/tile and no spills (v4: 292->258 us). (3) The combine is distributed after a grid barrier and costs 3-4 us. The ticket combine re-read partials already evicted from L2 by the KV stream and cost +47-84 us on the critical path. (4) It was raced against master's actual FA3 call on the same SM, which no earlier loop was. So it is not the same mechanism again, and prior is set correctly: the metadata fold kept FA3, this replaces it. WEAKEST LINK, the H100->H200 transfer. On the H100 the gate is effectively math-bound: math-only 233 us (v32) / 119-121 (v16) equals the loads-only time, and mainloop = math + about 26 us / 18 us of issue-slot and barrier contention from load-issue instructions. Both terms are per-SM and do not shrink on the H200 (same GH100 SM count and clocks). The H200's 4.8 vs 3.35 TB/s helps FA3, which is memory-parallelism-bound but still latency/HBM-sensitive: its main kernel already gains 1.13-1.15x (322->285.9, 170.9->148.6). It barely helps the gate. Estimate: gate mainloop on the H200 about 240-259 (v32) / 125-139 (v16), plus about 11-13 us combine/launch, against master's call of about 295 / 158. That gives e2e 0.86-0.92 (v32) and 0.87-0.95 (v16). v16 can miss the 0.95 bar. The H100's 0.82 is therefore an upper bound on the gain, not the expected value. Rough headline at r=0.875 on both rows (full verify about 0.79 / 0.74 of those loads, inferred from the 13.2% / 12.4% shares): about +1.7% (v32) + 1.5% (v16) = about 3.2%. Pessimistic, with only v32 routed at 0.92: about 1.3%. p(>=2.5% headline) is nearer 0.35 than 0.4, putting EV at about 1.1-1.4. That is marginal against the 1.5 bar, but the race makes the loss case free apart from the check. The pre-registered fa3gate rule (mainloop >= 2.6 TB/s) was NOT met (2.52). Proceeding rests on CLAIMS.md:86, after WS was closed (fa3ws/fa3math, 0.78-0.83x of the gate's math). Not a defect, but the build log must make the H200 reading interpretable (see open_questions). The expected shapes are consistent: only v16/v32 full move, verify_1 is excluded (1.42x loss, latency-bound combine), and sliding is untouched.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing + paired-heads-launch-cleanup (+ ab-tune-batch-gate, patches in done/gain and done/neutral): on full verify B>1, master's fused pre-attention writes q in the PADDED/PAIRED layout for FA3's head-paired call, and _paired_norm_gate_kernel reads FA3's paired output layout. The gate kernel writes the plain [B,8,16,64] bf16 layout (out[((b*8+t)*HQ + hh*8+gq)*D]). The build must either read master's paired q and write the layout the paired norm-gate expects, or switch both endpoints for the routed rows. Otherwise there is an extra pad/unpad launch or a wrong-layout epilogue. That hits correctness, or eats several us of the margin, which the node e2e (call-to-call) did not include. Print which q/out layouts and which norm-gate kernel are used on routed rows.

fused-preattention-triton (and the v3 fused pre-attention prologue): this kernel writes the new K/V at cache_loc before attention. The gate reads the cache right after, so ordering must stay in-stream (no PDL early trigger into the gate launch, see rules_flags). Otherwise the gain is independent.

Not confounding: the sliding, decode and full decode_1/verify_1 landings (stream-K, cluster, onepass, s2b/sw17). Their rows are untouched and their kernels are not routed through this path. The sw17 gate 'flips between runs' (CLAIMS.md:60), so sliding verify_32 can move about 1-3% on its own. Read the full verify_16/32 rows from the profile, not the headline.
interference: No companion needed. The change is routed per row by its own in-prepare race against master's FA3 path, and the build prints per-row, per-round ratios and errors. The judge profile then attributes any movement directly to the full verify_16 / verify_32 rows, and the race itself is the control. If the race does not route, the run still yields the first H200 measurement of the gate's mainloop and of FA3 at v16/v32 (provided the diagnostics below are printed), which is the information the next decision needs. An ab-revert of the pairing landings would not make the single result any less ambiguous; it is a layout-integration question for the build, not an interaction effect.
rules_flags: Grid barrier without a co-residency guarantee (plain <<<>>> launch, spin on an arrive counter until == G). If fewer than G CTAs can be resident on the judge GPU, a timed graph replay hangs and the run times out (charged). That can happen if occupancy differs from 2/SM (smem carve-out, reg count after the integration edits), if the SM count differs, or if any CTA of another kernel is still resident through a PDL/programmatic-serialization edge. Required: G = 2 x the device's multiProcessorCount (not a hard-coded 132), and an assert in prepare that cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor >= 2, else route master. Launch WITHOUT any programmatic stream serialization attribute, and do not let the preceding pre-attention kernel's PDL trigger overlap it. Preferably use a cooperative launch (cudaLaunchAttributeCooperative / cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, capturable in CUDA 12+ graphs), which fails loudly instead of hanging.

Self-resetting counters: the last departing CTA resets arrive/depart with plain stores at kernel end. That is safe for stream-ordered replays only. Use a counter buffer per routed row (v16, v32) zeroed once in prepare, never shared with any other launch, and never on a side stream. If a prepare race iteration raises or aborts, re-zero the counters before graph capture.

Page size and scales: the kernel hard-codes page_size 1 and ignores k_scale/v_scale (it takes only the softmax scale). Tests use page_size 64 and kv_scale 1/64. Gate the route on config page_size == 1 and config kv_scale == 1 (both are config, so branching is legal), plus window == 0, q_len 8, Hq 16, Hkv 2, D 64, B in {16, 32}. Otherwise fall back to master. Never branch on the k_scale/v_scale tensor values.

Fresh inputs: lens and the page table are read on device each call (warp-0 prefix scan in the prologue), which is good. The partials buffer (G+B slots x 128 rows x 64 fp32 + m/l) and the counters must be allocated in prepare from config/shape only. Nothing input-derived may be cached across calls, and nothing may be allocated in kernel_fn. The lens read assumes B <= 64, which holds.

Precision is fine: queries rounded to FP8 E4M3 as FA3 does. P is f16 (finer than FA3's FP8 P), V is widened to f16 exactly, and O accumulates in fp32. Keep the cp.async->wgmma fence.proxy.async: the fenceless variants were faster but formally racy. 'Passed the check' does not make them safe.

Every key: stream-K covers all 64-key tiles of every request and masks the tail tile. The judge-metric check on judge inputs covers it, but the prepare self-check must use the problem's own lengths spread (agentic) with tail lengths that are not multiples of 64.
Self-check must not import reference.py (rejected). Use the submission's own fp64 reference and its own FP8-query-rounded reference for the judge-style metric.

Build: load_inline of the 2100-line fa3gate.cu as-is compiles every lineage kernel (v1-v6, MODE/F/NS templates, g_dbg/globaltimer instrumentation). Strip to the v6 MODE-1 NS=3 instantiation (plus optional diag modes), drop the debug globals, compile with -gencode arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a in a background thread, and fall back to master if the build fails or has not finished by the time the race must start. The whole run has 15 min including master's existing builds.
freshness: E checked. BEST 1.6340 (job 4e386647edd845f7), blob 2eb03f76, both equal to mint, moved 0.00% vs a 1.24% margin: fresh. CLAIMS.md:86 [lead] is the newest claim for the mechanism; its reopen is this exact judge check at v16/v32 full (it also suggests stacking the [shelf] metadata fold CLAIMS.md:82 for verify_1, which this hypothesis omits; optional, not a hold). CLAIMS.md:85 and :84 are [node-only]. The proceed rule for node-only ('per-SM work transfers, HBM rates do not') is met in substance: the gate's H200 advantage rests on its per-SM math floor (233/120 us) being below the judge's FA3 main (285.9/148.6 us), not on an HBM rate. CLAIMS.md:63 [refuted] s7 has the reopen 'an isolated DIAG beats FA3's main loop at B=16 and B=32 first'. That is met on the node, same process (259 vs 322, 137-139 vs 167-171 us), not yet on the H200. The prepare race is exactly that test on the judge GPU, so not a hold. CLAIMS.md:53 [refuted] FA3 call-site tweaks is a different mechanism. CLAIMS.md:40 [landed] FA3 pairing owns these rows, and this replaces it on master's live base, so it is not stale.
open_questions: What the build MUST print (the [fvg] block plus PATH CHOSEN lines that survive the 16 KB log tail). Build s and whether it finished before the race. From cudaFuncGetAttributes: numRegs, localSizeBytes (spill, must be 0), static+dynamic smem. Occupancy blocks/SM (must be 2), multiProcessorCount and G. Per row and round: master call us, gate e2e us, ratio, fp64 relL2 vs fp32, judge-style metric and worst row vs bound. The route decision with the reason. ALSO, if build time allows, a one-shot H200 diagnostic: gate mainloop-only (MODE 0), math-only and loads-only us with the implied TB/s at v16/v32. That is the H200 gather ceiling and the math floor, the two numbers the node could not supply, and they decide whether a v16-fails/v32-passes outcome is the math floor (stop) or contention (tunable).

Does master's paired q/output layout on full verify B>1 match what the gate reads and writes? If not, which side is adapted, and is its cost inside the race timing? (The race runs through kernel_fn, so it is, but the node's 0.82 did not include it.)
Is the 0.95 bar applied per row independently? v16 could plausibly sit at 0.90-0.96 on the H200. Routing v32 alone is still worth about 1.3-1.7%.

The per-SM CTA priority imbalance (lower-id CTA finishes about 20% earlier) should be the same on the H200 scheduler. A priority-aware static split (<= 2% modelled) is the cheapest follow-up if the gate routes but barely.

Value estimate: H200 transfer likely gives r about 0.86-0.92, not 0.82-0.85. Re-derive value_gain to about 2-3.5% when logging the result, so the outcome is not scored as a miss against an inflated 4.2%.
